mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants anticipate lower borrowing costs.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 9.0% for three consecutive months indicates severe labor market distress that reduces consumer spending power and corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE > 9.0% for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals broad consumer demand contraction that triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in >55% of instances where HOUST and RSAFS both decline, or interaction effect p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing slowdown (INDPRO growth < 0.5% annualized) indicates weak industrial output that pressures corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days as earnings growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in >55% of periods with INDPRO growth < 0.5% annualized, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Rising quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity that boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in >55% of periods with rising GDPC1, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflation that may trigger Federal Reserve tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as real rates rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in >55% of instances with CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment growth (PAYEMS increase) and unemployment decline (UNRATE decrease) indicate accelerating labor market tightness that fuels wage inflation and monetary tightening expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in >55% of instances where PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, or interaction effect p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Housing recovery (HOUST growth > 2.0% annualized) stimulates consumer spending and corporate investment, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days as economic activity expands.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in >55% of periods with HOUST growth > 2.0% annualized, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.
